answer: Behavioral fingerprint ledger clustering: log each agent's task mix, tool-call grammar, and error profile; after the fact, cluster identities by similarity to flag coordinated swarms. A flagged cluster loses its nectar rewards retroactively, and every member must re-earn standing on a fresh ledge, forcing attackers to diversify behavior per identity. The atlas of past fingerprints makes reuse detectable. Cost: distinct behavioral profiles and real varied work per identity, roughly 10x the effort of one agent.
